hints: Define the normal random variable $X \sim \mathrm{N}(9.5, 1.3^2)$ where $\mu = 9.5$ and $\sigma = 1.3$.
Standardise the value $X = 10.2$ using the formula $Z = \dfrac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$.
Use the upper-tail identity $\mathrm{P}(Z > z) = 1 - \Phi(z)$, look up $\Phi(z)$ in the normal distribution table, and round to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Let $X$ denote the time in minutes Peter takes to walk to the shop and buy a newspaper. We are given:
$$X \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu, \sigma^2) \quad \text{with } \mu = 9.5 \text{ and } \sigma = 1.3$$
We need to find the probability that he takes longer than $10.2$ minutes, written as $\mathrm{P}(X > 10.2)$.

Start with the standardisation formula:
$$Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$$
Substitute $X = 10.2$, $\mu = 9.5$, and $\sigma = 1.3$:
$$Z = \frac{10.2 - 9.5}{1.3}$$
Subtract in the numerator:
$$10.2 - 9.5 = 0.7$$
Divide by $1.3$:
$$Z = \frac{0.7}{1.3} \approx 0.53846$$

Rewrite the probability in terms of the standard normal variable $Z$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 10.2) = \mathrm{P}(Z > 0.5385)$$

Since the normal distribution table gives the area to the left, $\Phi(z)$, and total area is 1, use the complement rule for the upper tail:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > 0.5385) = 1 - \Phi(0.5385)$$

Look up $z = 0.5385$ in the standard normal distribution table:
$$\Phi(0.538) = 0.7047, \quad \text{table entry for } 0.5385 \approx 0.7046$$
Subtract from 1:
$$1 - 0.7046 = 0.2954$$
Round to 3 significant figures:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 10.2) \approx 0.295$$

hints: Write the condition as a probability statement: $\mathrm{P}(X > t) = 0.90$, which implies $\mathrm{P}(X < t) = 0.10$.
Because $\mathrm{P}(X < t) = 0.10 < 0.5$, the cutoff $t$ lies below the mean $\mu = 9.5$, corresponding to a negative standard normal score $z$.
Find the critical value for an area of $0.90$ from the critical values table ($\Phi(1.282) = 0.90$), giving $z = -1.282$.
Set up the standardisation equation $\dfrac{t - 9.5}{1.3} = -1.282$ and solve for $t$ to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
We are told that Peter takes longer than $t$ minutes on 90% of days. In probability notation:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > t) = 0.90$$
Because total probability is 1, the probability that he takes less than $t$ minutes is:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < t) = 1 - 0.90 = 0.10$$

Since $0.10 < 0.5$, $t$ must be smaller than the mean $\mu = 9.5$. This means the corresponding standard normal $Z$-score is negative:
$$z < 0$$

Look up the probability $0.90$ in the critical values table for the normal distribution:
$$\Phi(1.282) = 0.9000$$
Because our value is in the lower 10% tail, attach a negative sign:
$$z = -1.282$$

Start with the standardisation formula:
$$Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$$
Substitute $Z = -1.282$, $X = t$, $\mu = 9.5$, and $\sigma = 1.3$:
$$-1.282 = \frac{t - 9.5}{1.3}$$

Multiply both sides by $1.3$ to clear the denominator:
$$-1.282 \times 1.3 = t - 9.5$$
Calculate the product:
$$-1.6666 = t - 9.5$$
Add $9.5$ to both sides to solve for $t$:
$$t = 9.5 - 1.6666 = 7.8334$$
Round to 3 significant figures:
$$t = 7.83\text{ minutes}$$

hints: Find the single-day probability $\mathrm{P}(X < 8.8)$ by standardising $8.8$.
Notice the symmetry: $8.8$ is $9.5 - 0.7$, which yields $z = -0.5385$. By symmetry, this lower-tail probability equals the upper-tail probability found in part (i), which is $0.2954$.
Multiply this probability by $365$ days to calculate the estimated number of days, and give the final answer as an integer.
walkthrough:
First, calculate the probability that Peter takes less than 8.8 minutes on any single randomly chosen day, $\mathrm{P}(X < 8.8)$. Standardise $X = 8.8$:
$$Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma} = \frac{8.8 - 9.5}{1.3}$$
Subtract in the numerator:
$$8.8 - 9.5 = -0.7$$
Divide by $1.3$:
$$Z = \frac{-0.7}{1.3} \approx -0.5385$$

Notice that $8.8$ is exactly $0.7$ units below the mean ($9.5 - 0.7 = 8.8$), whereas $10.2$ in part (i) was $0.7$ units above the mean ($9.5 + 0.7 = 10.2$). By the symmetry of the normal curve:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 8.8) = \mathrm{P}(Z < -0.5385) = \mathrm{P}(Z > 0.5385)$$
From part (i), this probability was:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 8.8) = 0.2954$$

To find the estimated number of days in a full year of 365 days, multiply the single-day probability by 365:
$$\text{Expected days} = 365 \times \mathrm{P}(X < 8.8)$$
Substitute $0.2954$:
$$\text{Expected days} = 365 \times 0.2954 = 107.821$$
(Using $0.295$: $365 \times 0.295 = 107.675$)

Because the question asks for a count of days, round to an integer without decimals:
$$\text{Estimated days} = 108 \quad (\text{or } 107)$$
